previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a male with a history of orthotopic liver transplant, chronic kidney disease, gastrostomy dependence, and chronic anemia, was admitted after outpatient labs revealed a hemoglobin of 6.5. He reported mild lightheadedness but denied chest pain, shortness of breath, or signs of acute bleeding. He received two units of packed red blood cells during the admission, with hemoglobin rising from 6.5 to 7.1 post-transfusion. His anemia was attributed to chronic disease, consistent with prior evaluations, and iron studies supported this diagnosis. He remained stable throughout the stay, with no complications from transfusions. His liver function was normal, immunosuppressive medications were continued, and chronic conditions were managed without change. He was discharged home with services, following up with the liver clinic for ongoing care.

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is a ___ year old male with a history of EtOH 
cirrhosis (status post transplant in ___ now on MMF & 
prednisone) and history of failure to thrive with intractable 
nausea requiring placement of a G-tube in ___ admitted for 
dehydration and acute kidney injury.

# Dehydration with acute on chronic kidney injury: Patient was 
found to have a creatinine to 3.2 from recent baseline 1.3-1.6 
on outpatient labs. He did note increasing frequency of diarrhea 
over the last week and poor oral intake over this time. Aside 
from malaise, patient denied any other constitutional symptoms 
and initial vitals were stable and he was without leokocytosis 
on CBC. On physical exam, he appeared volume depleted and was 
hydrated with 4L of NS with normalization of  creatine to recent 
baseline. His initial urine elecytrolytes were also consistent 
with pre-renal etiology. A urine culture returned E coli which 
may have also been contributing to the renal injury. He was 
started on ceftriaxone and was transitioned to cefpodoxime to 
complete a ___hronic diarrhea: Patient has chronic diarrhea of unclear 
etiology and promoted a worsening of his diarrhea over the last 
several days. This most likely contributed to his acute kidney 
injury above. He does have an ileo-colonic anastomosis and thus  
little to no large bowel to absorb water on chronic basis which 
most likely contributes to chronic diarrhea. Stool studies, 
including C.diff and ova/parasites were normal. CMV viral load 
is undetectable. A colonoscopy showed normal mucosa and and 
biopsies are pending. As patient had a ileocolonic anastomosis, 
it was likely that the patient's chronic diarrhea is related to 
the paucity of large bowel to reabsorb water. His MMF dosing was 
also decreased from 1000mg to 500mg BID as this can sometimes 
cause chronic diarrhea. HIs opium tincture was continued. 
Loperamide TID was also started on discharge as well.

# Anemia: Mr. ___ has a history of normocytic chronic anemia 
with low retic count.  His iron studies are consistent with 
chronic disease with low TIBC and high ferritin. He has been 
transfusion dependent over last seveal years and received 2 
units of PRBC this admission. He has been on EPO as an 
outpatient with minimal improvement. His lysis labs, B12, and 
folate were normal. Hematology saw him as an inpatient and would 
like to defer any further workup to outpatient, at which time a 
bone marrow biopsy can be considered. A colonscopy was normal as 
noted above.

#Hyponatremia: Patients sodium was below baseline on admission 
and improved with IV hydration. Most likley secondary to 
hypovolemia. 

# Etoh cirrhosis s/p OLT in ___: Liver function was stable this 
admission lowering concern for rejection. He has remained sober 
since ___. His MMR dosing was decreased from 1000mg to 500mg  
BID and prednisone 5mg was continued.  

# Chronic pain: Patient continues to have chronic neck pain 
secondary to cervical spine injury. He was continued on 
hydromorphone and oxycontin. At time of discharge, patient 
Oxycontin was increased to 30mg q12h for worsening neck pain 
(related to spinal hardware).
